summary: Cass Marshall previews Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader, a CRPG from Owlcat Games in which the player is a freelance explorer-captain in the Koronus Expanse. The review praises the characters, lore, writing, turn-based ground combat and moral choices, and calls it a detailed homage to the Fantasy Flight Games 40K RPGs. It criticizes the slow-drip leveling, a punishing Act 1 boss and clunky turn-based voidship combat. Overall the reviewer is hooked and sees it as a treat for 40K fans.
one_line: Polygon's impressions of Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader, a lore-rich Owlcat CRPG with great characters and choices, marred by pacing, a tough boss and clunky ship combat.
key_facts: Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader will be released on Dec. 7 on Windows PC and was reviewed with a pre-release code from Owlcat Games.
Rogue Trader is a computer role-playing game in the vein of Baldur's Gate 3 or Pillars of Eternity, with a custom protagonist whose stats and bonuses depend on backstory and home world.
The game has three major story paths: Dogmatic (exalts the God-Emperor), Heretical (pursues corruptive power) and Ionoclast (closest to modern-day 'good guy' morality).
The player trek around planets of the Koronus Expanse to get a new Navigator, repair the voidship and avoid diplomatic incidents; the voidship is the size of a modern city.
Combat is turn-based on a grid with cover and friendly fire, similar to Baldur's Gate 3 or XCOM 2; the reviewer's Rogue Trader is a sniper who relies on her Senechal at the front.
Companions include Abelard (Senechal, morally poor but loyal, former Imperial Navy), Augusta (Sister of Battle), Cassia (Navigator), Pasqal (Tech-Priest) and Marazhai Aezyrraesh.
Marazhai Aezyrraesh is a dark space elf who feeds off the suffering of sentient beings and is the reviewer's favorite companion.
The game is an homage to Fantasy Flight Games' Warhammer 40K RPGs, including Rogue Trader and Dark Heresy; Owlcat Games has paid close attention to detail in the Koronus Expanse.
Locations include ancient tech-priest facilities, the xenos city of Commorragh and cities honoring the God-Emperor of Mankind.
By the end of the first chapter the reviewer had leveled up 16 times, with marginal rewards per level like slightly farther movement or higher parry chance.
An incredibly tough boss at the end of Act 1 blocked progress and the player cannot leave to grind experience; the reviewer beat it by focusing on melee fighters' positioning.
Voidship naval combat is turn-based and the reviewer finds it clunky, annoyed by continually rotating the ship and setting up zones of attack.
